name: GoPro, Inc.

profile.description: GoPro designs and sells action cameras (HERO and MAX lines), mounts and accessories, and a subscription service bundling cloud storage, camera replacement and the Quik editing app. The founder-led company has seen revenue fall from $1.16B in 2021 to $652M in 2025, and Q2 2026 revenue dropped another 31% to about $105M while subscription revenue rose 11% to $29M (28% of sales). On May 11, 2026 the board launched a strategic review including a possible sale or merger (advised by Houlihan Lokey). The stock trades below $1, and GoPro has received a Nasdaq minimum-bid-price deficiency notice.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): GoPro's main business-model evolution is its subscription service, now $29M per quarter (28% of Q2 2026 revenue) with a record 69% attach rate, and it has recently explored defense and aerospace markets with Oliver Wyman [1][2]. The core camera franchise is shrinking. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI product launches or quantified AI savings were found in research. Market Share (1/2): GoPro still won a February 2026 ITC exclusion order against three Insta360 camera models, but camera units shipped fell 51.7% in Q2 2026, showing share loss to Insta360 and DJI [1][4]. Pipeline (0/2): GoPro withdrew full-year 2026 guidance and disclosed no dated next-gen products [2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D of $126.8M was 19.5% of FY2025 revenue, well above consumer-electronics peers, though it is down 32% from $185.9M in 2024 [5].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): GoPro's long-standing purpose of helping the world capture and share itself in immersive and exciting ways is specific and distinctive, and founder-CEO Nick Woodman has championed it since the company's founding [1]. Community Impact (0/2): No current charitable programs with measurable impact were found in research. Employee Retention (0/2): Headcount is now just 636 and R&D spending fell 32% in 2025, consistent with repeated downsizing; no retention data was found [5]. Insider Buying (1/2): FMP records one large acquisition (about 19.3M shares) logged as a purchase in Q3 2026 against two sales in Q2 2026, but the buyer and context could not be verified, so this is scored as neutral [6].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on the Growth weighting. Every available metric scores at the floor: ROE of -497% and a profit margin of -28.5%, revenue down 31.3% YoY and a five-year revenue CAGR of -6.1% ($892M in 2020 to $652M in 2025), and a negative forward P/E (-93) that scores 0 [3][5]. Stockholders' equity is negative (-$32.7M at June 30, 2026, against $86M of debt), so D/E is not meaningful and is excluded. The provider-reported PEG of 0.73 rests on negative trailing and forward EPS (-$0.98 / -$0.01), so it is scored 0, in line with the negative-forward-P/E rule [3][5]. Weighted 0/9 = 0. The liquidity floor is passed at ~$32M per day ($0.93 x 34.4M shares).

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): A rugged camera physically capturing real-world footage cannot be replaced by software, and analysts attribute GoPro's decline to Insta360/DJI competition, smartphones and tariffs rather than to AI [1][4]. Some long-term exposure exists because AI-native editing in competitors' apps and smartphones could erode the value of GoPro's Quik subscription. AI Opportunity (0/1): No quantifiable AI revenue.

infinite_game.summary: GoPro began with a genuine founder's cause, but by Sinek's measure it is now playing a survival game: revenue has fallen roughly 44% since 2021, R&D and headcount have been cut sharply, and the board is shopping the company. The subscription pivot shows adaptability, but the enterprise's endurance is now in question.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The founding vision of helping people capture and share their lives is authentic, but it has not shaped a durable strategy, and the May 2026 strategic review shows the institution itself is now for sale [2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Headcount of just 636 and a 32% cut in R&D spending in 2025 signal repeated downsizing, and the pending sale process adds uncertainty for employees [2][5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): GoPro's main response to Insta360 has been litigation, including ITC exclusion orders and district-court patent suits, while Insta360 has countersued in China; this is a fight to block a rival rather than learn from it [4].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): GoPro shifted toward a subscription model (28% of revenue, 69% attach rate) and has explored defense and aerospace applications, a meaningful but not transformative adaptation [1][2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Woodman kept R&D near 20% of revenue and enforced GoPro's IP against a much larger rival [4][5]. However, the cuts and the turn to a sale process reflect the constraints of a balance sheet with negative equity [3].

investment_thesis: The only constructive case is optionality: the board is running a formal sale process with Houlihan Lokey after receiving several unsolicited inbound inquiries, and GoPro still owns a globally recognized brand, a subscription business growing 11% with a 69% attach rate, and a design patent the ITC upheld against Insta360 [1][2][4]. At a ~$200M market cap, a strategic buyer could value the brand, the IP and the defense/aerospace adjacency above the current price.
thesis_continued: Fundamentals are deteriorating fast: Q2 2026 revenue fell 31% to ~$105M, camera units fell 51.7%, the GAAP net loss widened to $51M, and adjusted EBITDA was -$29M [1]. Stockholders' equity is negative (-$32.7M) with only $27M of cash against $86M of debt, the stock faces Nasdaq delisting below $1, and any sale could come at a price that leaves little for common shareholders [3][5].
key_catalysts: Outcome of the strategic review launched May 11, 2026 (sale or merger via Houlihan Lokey)
Enforcement of the February 2026 ITC exclusion order on Insta360 Ace, Ace Pro and Ace Pro 2 cameras
Regaining Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance within the 180-day window
key_risks: Liquidity stress: $27M cash versus $86M debt and negative stockholders' equity
Continued hardware collapse (Q2 2026 hardware revenue -40%, units -51.7%) as Insta360 and DJI gain share
Nasdaq delisting or a sale below the current price that wipes out common equity value
